summary: Reviewed pm.py. _build_pm_prompt() correctly returns: a brief imperative opener, project_path, plan_file label, injection-safety warning, separator, and verbatim full plan document content. OSError on missing plan file is handled gracefully with an embedded message rather than a crash. No identity declarations, no enumerated steps. Architecture is correct — PM is the only node that legitimately needs to embed external file content in the user-turn prompt, and it does so cleanly. All four acceptance criteria confirmed PASS. Ruff independently verified clean.

comments.note: The OSError fallback in _build_pm_prompt() (`plan_content = f'[Could not read plan file at {plan_path}: {exc}]'`) is a good defensive pattern. The error message is embedded inline in the prompt rather than raising, which allows the agent to see the failure context and self-report rather than crashing the node. This is idiomatic for this codebase.

pm.py is correctly distinct from the six pipeline-stage nodes: it legitimately embeds external file content (the plan document) in the user-turn prompt, whereas all other nodes carry only runtime context. This asymmetry is intentional and well-reasoned — the PM needs the plan text; other agents fetch WP details from the ledger via MCP tools.

The module docstring (lines 1-14) still refers to 'injects only immediate runtime context (project path, injection-safety warning, and the plan document content)' in a way that could be misread as saying the prompt was always minimal. A minor clarification noting that identity and workflow guidance were moved to the persona system prompt in this WP would help future maintainers understand the history.
